exercices.nom: 45 Degree Leg Press Shoulder Width Stance
exercices.description:
Using a 45 degree leg press machine, take a seat and place your feet at a shoulder width stance.
Gently press the foot plate away from you as you unhook the lock bars. You will take the weight at this point, ensure your knees are not locked and your joints remain slightly flexed. This will be your starting position.
As you inhale, slowly lower the platform until your upper and lower legs make a 90-degree angle.
As you exhale, press through your heels to push the foot plate away from you, engaging your quadriceps and glutes in order to do so.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and ensure to lock the safety pins properly once you are done.

Caution: Always securely lock the safety bars once you have finished.

Variations: Barbell Squats or Dumbbell Squats.

 Have your partner hold your feet or ankles. Abduct your legs as far as you can. This will be your starting position.

 Now, relax the muscles in your legs as your partner pushes your feet apart, stretching as far as is comfortable for you. Be sure to let your partner know when the stretch is adequate to prevent overstretching or injury.

exercices.nom: Alternating Dumbbell Press Up Renegade Rows
exercices.description:
1) Start in a high plank position with a dumbbell in each hand.
2) Perform a push-up, then row one dumbbell up towards your hip while balancing on the opposite hand.
3) Lower the dumbbell back down and repeat on the other side.
4) Continue alternating rows while maintaining a stable plank position keeping the hips still.
5) Focus on keeping your core engaged and hips level throughout the exercise.

exercices.description:
Position your body on the vertical leg raise bench so that your forearms are resting on the pads next to the torso and holding on to the handles.  Your arms will be bent at a 90 degree angle.

	 The torso should be straight with the lower back pressed against the pad of the machine and the legs extended pointing towards the floor.  This will be your starting position.

	 Now as you breathe out, lift your legs up as you keep them extended.  Continue this movement until your legs are roughly parallel to the floor and then hold the contraction for a second.  Tip: Do not use any momentum or swinging as you perform this exercise.

	 Slowly go back to the starting position as you breathe in.

	 Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Variations: As you become more advanced you can start to rotate your pelvis forward at the top of the movement to really engage the lower abs. You may also straighten your legs to increase the difficulty of this movement.

Keep your arms extended and your back straight, in fact, from your head to your feet should be one straight line. This will be your starting position.To initiate the movement, exhale and pull your body upward by contracting your lats (back muscles) and bending your elbows. Tip: Avoid swinging, twisting or jerking motions as you could cause yourself an injury.After a brief pause, inhale and return your body along the same path back into the starting position.Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.Variations: Horizontal Barbell Pull Up or Chin Ups.

Lay flat on a bench with a barbell in the rack above you. Take a medium grip (a grip which creates a 90 degree angle at your elbows half way through the movement) and lift the bar off the rack so that it is directly above your chest. Keep your elbows locked at this point for safety. This will be your starting position.
Whilst inhaling, start to lower the bar by bending at your elbows until the bar gently touches the middle of your chest.
After a brief pause, exhale and press the bar back into the starting position by contracting your pectoral muscles.
Repeat the movement for the recommended amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.

Caution: You should always have a spotter when attempting this movement. If a spotter is not available you should be conservative with the weight you are using.

Variations: Smith Machine Chest Press or Flat Dumbbell Chest Press.

Grab a mat and lay down flat on your back. Have your knees bent to create a 90 degree angle with your feet planted on the floor. Take hold of a barbell and keep it close to your chest. Tip: For this movement you may either need a partner to hold your feet down or gently place additional weights on your feet. This will be your starting position.
To initiate the movement, exhale and roll your shoulders up and off the mat by contracting your abdominal muscles whilst pressing the barbell directly towards the ceiling at the same time. Continue to sit up as you push the weight as high towards the ceiling as possible.
Once your arms are vertical and your abdominal muscles are as tight as they can be, pause briefly, inhale and return your body back along the same path into the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Variations: Otis-Up or Crunches.

(Importé de MyPTHub.)

Grab a loaded barbell and adopt a standing position with your feet shoulder width apart. Have your arms in front of you but still perpendicular to the floor (overhand grip, palms facing behind you). Slightly bend at your knees and maintain a straight back throughout. This will be your starting position.
Whilst keeping your knees stationary, inhale as you lean forwards from your waist (remember to keep a straight back), keeping the barbell close to you as you go. Keep lowering the barbell towards your feet until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
After a brief pause bring your torso upright again by pushing your hips forward. Tip: Remember, this whole movement is performed with 'stiff' legs (slight bend at the knee, but no more) and a straight back throughout. Exhale as you perform this part of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Caution: This is not an exercise for those with back issues. Avoid jerking motions as this could cause serious injury.

Variation: Dumbbell Stiff Legged Deadlift or Good Mornings.

Adopt a shoulder width stance with your arms in a comfortable position that will not aid in the movement. This will be your starting position.
Take a step forward (slightly larger than a normal step) and as you land, drop your body down so that you create two right angles at your knees. Inhale as you do so whilst maintaining a straight torso.
Make sure that you keep your front knee over your heel and not over your toes. Your front shin should now be perpendicular to the floor.
As you exhale, push off the floor with your rear foot to return your body into a standing position.
Alternate legs as you go (as you walk forwards) and repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Variations: Dumbbell Walking Lunges or Barbell Walking Lunges.

Stand upright with your arms beside your torso and adopt a shoulder width stance. This will be your starting position.
Inhale and descend into a press up position. Place your hands just wider than shoulder width and jump backward with your feet so that your legs are fully extended and your body is supported by your toes and hands.
Continue to drop your torso downward towards the floor by bending at your elbows until your chest is only a few inches away.
Once you get to this point, exhale and aggressively press through your hands by extending your elbow joints and create enough upward motion to be able to jump your legs back underneath your body so that when you take your hands off the floor, you should be in the bottom of a squat.
Now, press through the middle of your feet by using your thighs and glutes, extending at both your knee and hip joints to generate power for a jumping motion (you can use your arms at this point to emphasise lift).
As you land, inhale and go straight into the next repetition.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Grab a mat and lay down flat on your back. Extend your arms directly above your chest towards the ceiling and maintain their position throughout. For your lower body, create a 90 degree bend at both your hips and knee joints so your lower legs are parallel with the floor, feet in mid air. This will be your starting position.
To initiate the movement, inhale and extend one of your legs out and lower towards the floor as you go. Continue until your heel is an inch off the floor.
After a brief pause, exhale and return your leg back along the same path into the starting position.
Alternate as you go and repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Variations: Cocoons or Reverse Crunches.

To start this exercise kneel down just in front of a ledge or platform and lean forward so that you are now weight baring on your arms. Have your hands placed just outside of where your chest would be. Now you should come up onto your feet by stepping up onto the ledge or platform behind you so that your body is suspended above the floor. The only points of contact (with the floor) should be your hands and the platform itself. Grab a dumbbell in each hand and adopt a shoulder width stance. Without leaning backward or putting your posture into jeopardy, press one of the dumbbells above your head so that you arm is fully extended, yet slightly flexed/bent at your elbow. Make sure your palm is facing forward at this point. Allow your other arm to hang perpendicular to the floor by your side. This will be your starting position.
Slowly and in a controlled fashion, descend the dumbbell until it reaches the side of your head (parallel with your ear), creating a 90 degree angle at your elbow. Inhale throughout this motion and flare your elbow out wide.
After a brief pause, exhale and press the dumbbell back along this path to its starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Variations: Alternating Kettlebell Press or Arnold Press.
